system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:59 UTC, tara.nguyen created temp.jsmith; at 13:42:00 UTC, the account was added to the Contractors group. The name and group match the stated help-desk account-creation practice, so these events alone do not establish malicious account creation.

tara.nguyen connected by RDP from WS-TNGUYEN-01 to DC-LV-01, and the domain controller recorded an interactive logon for her. This conflicts with the stated practice that remote administration is only performed from WS-KORTEGA-01.
tara.nguyen later connected by RDP from WS-TNGUYEN-01 to FILE-LV-01, where an interactive logon was recorded. This is also inconsistent with the stated remote-administration practice.
On WS-TNGUYEN-01, tara.nguyen launched the Group Policy Management Console with a high-integrity token. The evidence does not show what actions, if any, were performed in it.

A UserAssist registry value contains a ROT13-encoded path to a Slack shortcut, suggesting Slack was launched or recorded in Explorer activity. Slack is not among the approved services listed in the environment context.
A later UserAssist registry value contains a ROT13-encoded path to powershell.exe, suggesting a PowerShell launch, but the record does not provide its command line or establish what it did.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy access logs were not collected from PROXY-LV-01 between 13:30 and 14:10 UTC because of a forwarder outage; this overlaps the observed Firefox connections to the proxy at 14:00 and 14:05 UTC. The destinations and activity behind those requests cannot be determined from the supplied evidence. Relevant connection records: S12-00025, S12-00030, S12-00031, S12-00034, S12-00037, S12-00050, S12-00052, S12-00062, S12-00067.
The supplied records do not show the contents of the RDP sessions, the actions taken in GPMC, or the command line or actions associated with the inferred PowerShell launch.
claims_not_established: Whether the RDP sessions and elevated GPMC use were authorized, or what actions were performed during them.
Whether temp.jsmith was requested by a contractor or whether any account activity after creation was malicious.
Whether the apparent Slack and PowerShell launches occurred as inferred from UserAssist, and what was done in either application.

Whether tara.nguyen accessed or changed the ReportSync job or its credentials.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the contractor request and change or service-desk records associated with temp.jsmith.
Obtain DC-LV-01 and FILE-LV-01 session, security, and administrative audit records for tara.nguyen's RDP sessions, including any account, group, policy, or scheduled-job changes.
Review available endpoint process, command-line, PowerShell, and interactive-session telemetry from WS-TNGUYEN-01 and the remotely accessed hosts.
Recover proxy access logs or equivalent browser/network records for 13:30–14:10 UTC to identify the destinations and activity associated with the Firefox connections.
Confirm with IT whether tara.nguyen was authorized to access either server or use elevated GPMC during the stated change window.
